chunks: This is a very fine and eloquent expression. It means that if we are not allowed our right we will be regarded humble. This sense comes out from this expression because on the rear part of the camel only slaves, prisoners or other people of this type used to ride.

key_terms.الرَّدِيف: The person riding on the rear of the camel
key_terms.الرِّدَاف: The rear part or hump of a camel, often where a slave or prisoner would ride
key_terms.حَقّنَا: Our right (referring to the rightful status of the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase regarding the 'radif' and humility in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī explains an eloquent phrase indicating that if the Ahl al-Bayt are denied their rightful status, they are considered humble or lowly. He illustrates this by noting that the 'radif' (the person riding on the rear/hump of a camel) was typically a slave, prisoner, or someone of lower status, implying that being denied one's right reduces one's standing to that of a subordinate.
